verses.original: שִׁלְחוּ־ כַ֥ר מֹשֵֽׁל־ אֶ֖רֶץ מִסֶּ֣לַע מִדְבָּ֑רָה אֶל־ הַ֖ר בַּת־ צִיּֽוֹן׃
verses.transliteration: šil·ḥū- ḵar mō·šêl- ’e·reṣ mis·se·la‘ miḏ·bā·rāh ’el- har baṯ- ṣî·yō·wn
verses.literal: Send the [tribute] lambs to the ruler of the land from Sela in the desert to the mount of Daughter Zion

verses.original: וְהָיָ֥ה כְעוֹף־ נוֹדֵ֖ד מְשֻׁלָּ֑ח קֵ֣ן תִּֽהְיֶ֙ינָה֙ בְּנ֣וֹת מוֹאָ֔ב מַעְבָּרֹ֖ת לְאַרְנֽוֹן׃
verses.transliteration: wə·hā·yāh ḵə·‘ō·wp̄- nō·w·ḏêḏ mə·šul·lāḥ qên tih·ye·nāh bə·nō·wṯ mō·w·’āḇ ma‘·bā·rōṯ lə·’ar·nō·wn
verses.literal: - Like fluttering birds . . . pushed out of the nest so are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon

verses.original: הָבִיאוּ עֵצָה֙ עֲשׂ֣וּ פְלִילָ֔ה שִׁ֧יתִי צָהֳרָ֑יִם צִלֵּ֖ךְ בְּת֣וֹךְ כַלַּ֛יִל סַתְּרִי֙ נִדָּחִ֔ים אַל־ תְּגַלִּֽי׃ נֹדֵ֖ד
verses.transliteration: hå̄·ḇī·ʾū ‘ê·ṣāh ‘ă·śū p̄ə·lî·lāh šî·ṯî ṣā·ho·rā·yim ṣil·lêḵ bə·ṯō·wḵ ḵal·la·yil sat·tə·rî nid·dā·ḥîm ’al- tə·ḡal·lî nō·ḏêḏ
verses.literal: Give us counsel render a decision . . . Shelter us at noonday with shade . . . as dark as night Hide the refugees do not betray the one who flees

verses.original: נִדָּחַ֔י יָג֤וּרוּ בָךְ֙ הֱוִי־ סֵ֥תֶר לָ֖מוֹ מוֹאָ֛ב מִפְּנֵ֣י שׁוֹדֵ֑ד כִּֽי־ הַמֵּץ֙ אָפֵ֤ס שֹׁ֔ד כָּ֣לָה רֹמֵ֖ס תַּ֥מּוּ מִן־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
verses.transliteration: nid·dā·ḥay yā·ḡū·rū ḇāḵ hĕ·wî- sê·ṯer lā·mōw mō·w·’āḇ mip·pə·nê šō·w·ḏêḏ kî- ham·mêṣ ’ā·p̄ês šōḏ kā·lāh rō·mês tam·mū min- hā·’ā·reṣ
verses.literal: Let my fugitives stay with you be a refuge for Moab from the destroyer When the oppressor has gone destruction has ceased and the oppressors have vanished from the land

verses.original: בַּחֶ֙סֶד֙ כִּסֵּ֔א וְהוּכַ֤ן בְּאֹ֣הֶל דָּוִ֑ד שֹׁפֵ֛ט וְדֹרֵ֥שׁ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּמְהִ֥ר צֶֽדֶק׃ וְיָשַׁ֥ב עָלָ֛יו בֶּאֱמֶ֖ת
verses.transliteration: ba·ḥe·seḏ kis·sê wə·hū·ḵan bə·’ō·hel dā·wiḏ šō·p̄êṭ wə·ḏō·rêš miš·pāṭ ū·mə·hir ṣe·ḏeq wə·yā·šaḇ ‘ā·lāw be·’ĕ·meṯ
verses.literal: in loving devotion a throne will be established in the tent of David A judge seeking justice and hastening righteousness will sit on [it] in faithfulness

verses.original: שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ מוֹאָ֖ב גְאוֹן־ מְאֹ֑ד גֵּ֣א גַּאֲוָת֧וֹ וְעֶבְרָת֖וֹ וּגְאוֹנ֛וֹ בַּדָּֽיו׃ס לֹא־ כֵ֥ן
verses.transliteration: šā·ma‘·nū mō·w·’āḇ ḡə·’ō·wn- mə·’ōḏ gê ga·’ă·wā·ṯōw wə·‘eḇ·rā·ṯōw ū·ḡə·’ō·w·nōw bad·dāw lō- ḵên
verses.literal: We have heard of Moab’s pomposity his exceeding pride [and] conceit his overflowing arrogance But his boasting is empty . . .

verses.original: לָכֵ֗ן מוֹאָ֛ב יְיֵלִ֥יל יְיֵלִ֑יל כֻּלֹּ֣ה לְמוֹאָ֖ב תֶּהְגּ֖וּ לַאֲשִׁישֵׁ֧י קִיר־ חֲרֶ֛שֶׂת אַךְ־ נְכָאִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: lā·ḵên mō·w·’āḇ yə·yê·lîl yə·yê·lîl kul·lōh lə·mō·w·’āḇ teh·gū la·’ă·šî·šê qîr- ḥă·re·śeṯ ’aḵ- nə·ḵā·’îm
verses.literal: Therefore let Moab wail let them wail together for Moab Moan for the raisin cakes vvv of Kir-hareseth you who are utterly stricken

verses.original: כִּ֣י שַׁדְמוֹת֩ חֶשְׁבּ֨וֹן אֻמְלָ֜ל גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֗ה בַּעֲלֵ֤י גוֹיִם֙ הָלְמ֣וּ שְׂרוּקֶּ֔יהָ נָגָ֖עוּ עַד־ יַעְזֵ֥ר תָּ֣עוּ מִדְבָּ֑ר שְׁלֻ֣חוֹתֶ֔יהָ נִטְּשׁ֖וּ עָ֥בְרוּ יָֽם׃
verses.transliteration: kî šaḏ·mō·wṯ ḥeš·bō·wn ’um·lāl ge·p̄en śiḇ·māh ba·‘ă·lê ḡō·w·yim hā·lə·mū śə·rūq·qe·hā nā·ḡā·‘ū ‘aḏ- ya‘·zêr tā·‘ū miḏ·bār šə·lu·ḥō·w·ṯe·hā niṭ·ṭə·šū ‘ā·ḇə·rū yām
verses.literal: For the fields of Heshbon have withered along with the grapevines of Sibmah The rulers of the nations have trampled its choicest vines which had reached as far as Jazer and spread toward the desert Their shoots had spread out and passed over the sea

verses.original: עַל־ כֵּ֡ן אֶבְכֶּ֞ה בִּבְכִ֤י יַעְזֵר֙ גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֔ה אֲרַיָּ֙וֶךְ֙ חֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן וְאֶלְעָלֵ֑ה כִּ֧י דִּמְעָתִ֔י הֵידָ֥ד נָפָֽל׃ עַל־ קֵיצֵ֛ךְ וְעַל־ קְצִירֵ֖ךְ
verses.transliteration: ‘al- kên ’eḇ·keh biḇ·ḵî ya‘·zêr ge·p̄en śiḇ·māh ’ă·ray·yā·weḵ ḥeš·bō·wn wə·’el·‘ā·lêh kî dim·‘ā·ṯî hê·ḏāḏ nā·p̄āl ‘al- qê·ṣêḵ wə·‘al- qə·ṣî·rêḵ
verses.literal: So . . . I weep . . . with Jazer for the vines of Sibmah I drench Heshbon and Elealeh . . . with my tears Triumphant shouts have fallen silent over your summer fruit . . . and your harvest

verses.original: שִׂמְחָ֤ה וָגִיל֙ וְנֶאֱסַ֨ף מִן־ הַכַּרְמֶ֔ל לֹֽא־ יְרֻנָּ֖ן יְרֹעָ֑ע וּבַכְּרָמִ֥ים לֹ֣א יִדְרֹ֥ךְ הַדֹּרֵ֖ךְ יַ֗יִן בַּיְקָבִ֛ים לֹֽא־ הִשְׁבַּֽתִּי׃ הֵידָ֥ד
verses.transliteration: śim·ḥāh wā·ḡîl wə·ne·’ĕ·sap̄ min- hak·kar·mel lō- yə·run·nān yə·rō·‘ā‘ ū·ḇak·kə·rā·mîm lō yiḏ·rōḵ had·dō·rêḵ ya·yin bay·qā·ḇîm lō- hiš·bat·tî hê·ḏāḏ
verses.literal: Joy and gladness are removed from the orchard no one sings or shouts in the vineyards No one tramples . . . the grapes in the winepresses . . . I have put an end to the cheering

verses.original: עַל־ כֵּן֙ מֵעַ֣י יֶֽהֱמ֑וּ לְמוֹאָ֔ב כַּכִּנּ֖וֹר וְקִרְבִּ֖י לְקִ֥יר חָֽרֶשׂ׃
verses.transliteration: ‘al- kên mê·‘ay ye·hĕ·mū lə·mō·w·’āḇ kak·kin·nō·wr wə·qir·bî lə·qîr ḥā·reś
verses.literal: Therefore . . . my heart laments for Moab like a harp my inmost being vvv for Kir-heres

verses.original: וְהָיָ֧ה כִֽי־ מוֹאָ֖ב נִרְאָ֛ה עַל־ הַבָּמָ֑ה כִּֽי־ נִלְאָ֥ה וּבָ֧א אֶל־ מִקְדָּשׁ֛וֹ לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל וְלֹ֥א יוּכָֽל׃
verses.transliteration: wə·hā·yāh ḵî- mō·w·’āḇ nir·’āh ‘al- hab·bā·māh kî- nil·’āh ū·ḇā ’el- miq·dā·šōw lə·hiṯ·pal·lêl wə·lō yū·ḵāl
verses.literal: - When Moab appears on the high place when he wearies himself and enters . . . his sanctuary to pray it will do him no good

verses.original: זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְהוָ֛ה דִּבֶּ֧ר מֵאָֽז׃ אֶל־ מוֹאָ֖ב
verses.transliteration: zeh had·dā·ḇār ’ă·šer Yah·weh dib·ber mê·’āz ’el- mō·w·’āḇ
verses.literal: This is the message that the LORD spoke earlier concerning Moab

verses.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה יְהוָה֮ לֵאמֹר֒ דִּבֶּ֣ר בְּשָׁלֹ֤שׁ שָׁנִים֙ שָׂכִ֔יר כִּשְׁנֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב כְּב֣וֹד וְנִקְלָה֙ בְּכֹ֖ל הָרָ֑ב הֶהָמ֣וֹן וּשְׁאָ֥ר מְעַ֛ט מִזְעָ֖ר ל֥וֹא כַבִּֽיר׃ס
verses.transliteration: wə·‘at·tāh Yah·weh lê·mōr dib·ber bə·šā·lōš šā·nîm śā·ḵîr kiš·nê mō·w·’āḇ kə·ḇō·wḏ wə·niq·lāh bə·ḵōl hā·rāḇ he·hā·mō·wn ū·šə·’ār mə·‘aṭ miz·‘ār lō·w ḵab·bîr
verses.literal: And now the LORD . . . says In three years as a hired worker counts the years Moab’s splendor will become an object of contempt with all her many people And those who are left will be few . . . [and] feeble . . .
